indescribable

/in-dih-SKRY-buh-bul/ — stress on SKRY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indescribable describes something so extreme that ordinary words cannot fully capture it.

The chaos backstage in the final minute before the curtain rose was indescribable.

Example

After the final song, the standing ovation was so thunderous and emotional that the experience was utterly indescribable.

In (not) + describe + -able (can be done) = unable to be described with words. Describe is a full English word, so -able attaches directly (after dropping its silent e). The magnitude of emotion and applause literally exceeded what ordinary language could capture — truly unable to be put into words.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ineffable: Ineffable is reserved for what is too lofty or profound for words - deep joy, wonder, awe, the sacred. Indescribable is broader and plainer: it fits anything extreme that words cannot fully capture, even chaos or a disaster area. A sunrise over the canyon feels ineffable; the traffic after the game is merely indescribable.

unutterable: Unutterable means so extreme that speaking of it feels impossible or wrong - it usually attaches to grim things like unutterable horror, grief, or shame. Indescribable carries no such shadow: it simply says words fall short, whether the thing is wonderful, awful, or just overwhelming.

inexpressible: Inexpressible is for inner feelings that cannot be conveyed to anyone else - love, relief, longing held inside. Indescribable points outward as well as inward: scenes, noises, messes, and feelings can all be indescribable when ordinary words cannot do them justice.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

describable: able to be put into words

expressible: able to be conveyed in language

Where it sits · how far it goes beyond words

striking → remarkable → astonishing → indescribable

striking vs. indescribable: A striking view impresses you, but an indescribable one leaves you without words entirely.

remarkable vs. indescribable: A remarkable performance earns praise you can easily put into words, while an indescribable one defeats every word you try.

astonishing vs. indescribable: An astonishing discovery amazes you, but an indescribable feeling goes beyond what language can capture at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-: not — the same negating in- you met in morpheme unit M1 (Latin)

Root — describ(e): to write down, give an account of (Latin describere, from de- 'down' + scribere 'to write'); the silent e drops before -able (Latin)

Suffix — -able: able to be; capable of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together: describe + -able = 'able to be put into words,' and the in- you learned back in M1 flips it: Not able to be put into words — so extreme that ordinary words cannot capture it. This is your third meeting with this word: M1 spotlighted its in-, this card spotlights its -able, and Unit 28 (Communication, Writing & Storytelling) will teach it in full depth.

Use the root in a new word: descriptive: His descriptive essay made readers feel the salty wind of the harbor.

elevated; literary

Indescribable is the word when something is so extreme, profound, or overwhelming that ordinary language fails to capture it. Reach for it for emotional climaxes, natural phenomena, or experiences that defy typical vocabulary.
